transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-06-30 | Time: 10:00 AM PT | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE); Lina Gomez (Redwood SE); Alex Reed (Redwood CSM); Jessica Huang (AcmeFinance - Head of ML); Tom Brooks (AcmeFinance - Infra); Priya Menon (AcmeFinance - Secops); Evan Li (AcmeFinance - SRE)

Summary: Quick sync on current POC latency numbers, TTFT (time-to-first-token) vs streaming behavior, sequence length impacts, and kernel selection. Review of last week's changes (batching tweaks, kv cache warmup), decision on next kernel matrix, and next steps to run dedicated pool tests.

Topics:
- Current TTFT regressions after enabling secondary batching
- Streaming chunk sizes and tradeoffs for early token emission
- Sequence length patterns (256/512/1024) and perf cost
- Kernel selection, fused kernels vs fallback paths
- Security/residency questions for Private deployment tests

[00:00] Samir: Hey all, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Samir from Redwood, Lina our SE; Alex CSM; and from AcmeFinance Jessica, Tom, Priya, Evan. Can everyone hear me?
[00:10] Jessica: Yeah, good morning.
[00:12] Tom: Yep.
[00:20] Lina: Great. So last week we pushed the batching tweak and the KV warmup, and we saw mixed results visible in the dashboard. Samir, do you want to kick off with the numbers?
[00:32] Samir: Sure. So overall median TTFT dropped for small requests by about 12 percent on hosted, but for larger seq_len 512+ cases TTFT actually increased slightly — about 8 to 12 ms, likely due to the secondary batching window we introduced. Those are the highlights.
[01:05] Jessica: Hmm, that matches what we observed in the synthetic runs. Our user flows are usually 256 tokens but we have nightly jobs hitting 1024 occasionally, so that spike is concerning.
[01:17] Alex: Can you remind us of the batching policy parameters you used? I think there was a 15-ms secondary wait?
[01:25] Lina: Yeah, the policy was primary immediate dispatch with a 5-7ms micro-batching then a 15ms window for larger batch aggregation. The idea was to improve throughput for high qps.
[01:40] Tom: But that 15ms window adds to TTFT, right? Even if you improve throughput later. For our interactive flows TTFT matters more.
[01:50] Lina: Exactly; that's the tradeoff. We can tune the window or have adaptive rules: e.g., detect short sequences and bypass secondary batching. We started a simple heuristic but it needs more tuning.
[02:05] [02:05] Speaker 1: There's also the impact of kv cache warmup, I think the warm cache gives big wins but cold starts hit us hard.
[02:15] Samir: Right. Cold KV cache on new sessions shows TTFT regressions. We recommended pre-warming for the nightly batch jobs or using sticky sessions on dedicated pools.
[02:28] Jessica: Pre-warming is fine for batch, but for real-time we need the first token quick. Could streaming help? We started streaming but we saw jitter.
[02:40] Lina: Streaming helps TTFT because you can emit partial tokens earlier, but it depends on chunk size and tokenizer behavior. We saw better latency when emitting at 32-token chunks vs 64 in our tests on the Llama-variant. But there's also overhead from more gRPC frames.
[02:58] Evan: And we worry about partial outputs affecting downstream scoring. We have to make sure the reconstruction is stable.
[03:08] Tom: Also, on our side, we run mixed workloads — short chats and long generation jobs. We need a routing policy: route short chats to a low-latency pool and long jobs to throughput-optimized pool.
[03:20] Samir: Yep, smart routing is exactly what Redwood can do — route by seq_len or by intent. For the POC we can add a tag to sample traffic and route short queries to a dedicated low-latency profile. That would avoid the batching window.
[03:34] Jessica: That sounds useful. What's the cost delta?
[03:38] Samir: Roughly more expensive per request because smaller batch efficiency, but we can estimate — I'll send a spreadsheet with TTFT vs cost curves for the different profiles.
[03:48] Jessica: Good.
[03:50] [04:00] Lina: On kernel choices: we ran the fused attention kernel on our staging hardware and saw about 10–15 percent perf improvement for seq_len <=512. But for seq_len 1024 the memory pressure caused fallback to a conservative kernel which increased latency. We need to run a kernel selection matrix across sequence lengths and model variants.
[04:26] Tom: Can you clarify fallback? Is that automatic? We don't want unpredictable jumps in latency when fallback triggers.
[04:33] Lina: It's automatic — the runtime picks kernel based on available memory and kernel heuristics. We can pin kernels per model if you want deterministic behavior; that requires dedicated pool testing to ensure stability.
[04:45] Priya: From security perspective, pinning kernels on dedicated pool is fine as long as we keep audit logs and signatures. Also confirm KMS integration for Private.
[04:55] Samir: We'll include kernel pinning docs and the audit log behavior in the security packet.
[05:02] [05:10] Speaker 2: Quick question on streaming: what's the TTFT improvement we saw in the last run?
[05:15] Lina: For 256 token sequences, TTFT improved from ~65ms to ~42ms when we used 32-token streaming chunks and disabled the secondary batching for those requests. For 1024 seq, improvement was smaller because the chunking overhead grows.
[05:35] Jessica: Those numbers sound promising. But we also saw more variance — the p95 remained high with streaming.
[05:43] Lina: P95 is mostly due to GPU scheduling and kernel fallbacks. If we pin to low-latency kernels and isolate short-query pool on dedicated GPUs, p95 drops significantly.
[05:55] Tom: How long would it take for you to run the kernel matrix and share logs? We can spin up a 4 node staging if needed.
[06:03] Lina: I can run it in about 3 business days once the staging pool is provisioned — tests across seq_len 256/512/1024 and both quantized and fp16 variants. We'll capture TTFT, p50/p90/p95, and kernel trace.
[06:18] Samir: Great. Also want to highlight streaming protocol: if you need consistent outputs for scoring we can buffer a small lookahead before emitting but still beat TTFT. It's a tradeoff.
[06:30] [06:30] Speaker 3: There's a small transcription glitch: K V cache sometimes shows as K V cash in the notes.
[06:36] Alex: noted.
[06:38] Priya: On compliance, we need the SOC2 report and encryption-at-rest details for the dedicated pool. Also data residency confirmation for EU staging.
[06:48] Samir: We'll attach SOC2 and a short KMS/HSM integration doc. For EU residency we can provision region-specific infra; Lina can coordinate.
[06:59] Jessica: One more thing — can you run a synthetic that mimics early user flows (avg seq_len 180) and our nightly job (avg 900) and combine them in a 80/20 ratio? That would reflect real mixed workload.
[07:12] Lina: Yes, we'll run a mixed workload test on the staging dedicated pool once Tom provisions it.
[07:18] Tom: I'll try to have the pool ready by Friday 7/3.
[07:23] Samir: Perfect.
[07:25] [07:30] Alex: Cool. Let's go through the proposed next steps and owners. Samir will share the TTFT vs cost spreadsheet; Lina to run kernel matrix and mixed-workload test; Tom to provision the pool; Priya to confirm security questions.
[07:43] Jessica: Sounds good. Do we want a check-in next week same time?
[07:48] Samir: Yes, same time next Wednesday — 7/07 — to review kernel logs and results.
[07:55] Evan: We'll also provide trace IDs for a few outlier requests so you can correlate in your traces.
[08:02] Lina: Perfect, those will help.
[08:05] [08:10] Speaker 1: Quick note — competitors: Anthropic and Bedrock were mentioned as having different streaming behaviors; not a blocker but useful context.
[08:19] Samir: We'll include comparative notes but the focus is on deterministic low-latency for your interactive flows.
[08:27] Jessica: Thanks everyone.
[08:29] Samir: Thanks — will follow up with docs and spreadsheet. Meeting adjourned.

Recap / Action items (auto):
- Samir: Send TTFT vs cost spreadsheet + brief note on routing profiles (due 2026-07-02)

End of transcript.
